subject: journey/nautilus
prompt: Use case: illustration-story. A single landscape 3:2 illustration for the historical atlas sketchbook of Jules Verne's Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea. A nineteenth-century naturalist's field sketch in graphite and sepia pen with restrained transparent watercolour washes on warm ivory paper. Fine irregular parallel hatching, economical contour lines, a few details sharply observed; leave areas of cream paper around irregular unfinished edges. One coherent scene that reads at small sizes. No captions, labels, border, binding, signatures, photorealism, modern equipment, or Disney submarine designs. A small black pennant with one golden initial N unfurls from a pole beside a lone dark-coated Nemo on a low bare rock promontory. The setting sun rests on an ocean horizon interrupted by drift ice. Illustrate the imaginary open polar sea of Verne, no station, no other lettering.
